extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, area chairs, and editors involved with *ACL conferences (ACL, NAACL, EACL) and the TACL journal
extracted.subtask_description: Policies governing anonymization of submissions, reviewer conduct, and citation/ comparison expectations for submissions to *ACL conferences and the TACL journal (with date-sensitive provisions around a specified anonymity period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that submissions be anonymized
rubrics_metrics.description: *ACL conferences and TACL require that submissions be anonymized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions will be rejected if not properly anonymized. The intent is to maintain and protect double-blind review without sacrificing preprint publishing's benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity period and non-anonymized preprint prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission will not be considered anonymized if the authors post (or update) a non-anonymized preprint version within an anonymity period lasting from 1 month before the submission deadline until the time of notification (or withdrawal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule (as stated on the page) applied only to papers submitted for deadlines before January 12, 2024; the rest of that section applies only to such papers and the restrictions do not apply to papers submitted later, although authors are still cautioned against extensive advertising. The policy text: 'Submissions will be rejected if not properly anonymized.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymized preprints allowed during anonymity period (platform-dependent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymized preprints within the anonymity period are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currently this is only possible on certain platforms; ACL may consider using such a platform for all submissions in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-anonymized preprints posted before the anonymity period are allowed but must be declared
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-anonymized preprints before the anonymity period are allowed, although authors are encouraged to wait to post them until after the anonymity period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-anonymized preprint version exists, authors must declare its existence at submission time but should not cite it and are asked not to publicize it further during the anonymity period – the submitted paper should be as anonymous as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted preprint updates for correcting names
rubrics_metrics.description: ACL explicitly allows updates to preprints, at all times, for the sole purpose of correcting people’s names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the change falls within the required anonymous period of a conference, the PC Chairs should be notified of the correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / scope of 'preprint' for policy purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion of preprint is understood broadly to refer to any non-refereed paper posted online, including but not limited to preprint servers such as arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule applies only to preprints that authors post themselves, so it does not apply to (say) non-refereed proceedings volumes. The restriction on updating is intended to prevent authors from circumventing the rules by 'flag planting' with a placeholder version over 1 month in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct regarding author identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should be instructed not to actively try to discover the identity of the authors and not to let any suspicion or knowledge of author identity affect their judgment of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should not prevent reviewers from searching for related work, but they should take special care and postpone such searches until after they have read the paper completely and formed an initial impression of it. If a reviewer nevertheless uncovers the identity of the authors (or believes they can identify the authors for other reasons), they should inform the area chair or action editor (but not other reviewers) so that this information can be taken into account when making the final acceptance decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer disclosure of outside knowledge (post-Jan 12, 2024 change)
rubrics_metrics.description: After January 12, 2024, ACL reviewing procedures will explicitly ask reviewers to disclose any outside knowledge they may have about a submitted paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such disclosed information will be taken into account when assigning and using reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: General citation expectation: cite and credit relevant prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted to *ACL conferences and TACL should in principle cite and compare to all relevant prior work, regardless of when and how that work was presented to the community, and must credit work that influenced them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the general rule; specific qualifications (refereed priority, contemporaneous work window) follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of refereed publications over preprints for citation
rubrics_metrics.description: For citation, refereed publications take priority over preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to cite all refereed publications relevant to their submission, but may be excused for not knowing about all unpublished work (especially work that has been recently posted and/or is not widely cited). If a preprint has been superseded by a refereed publication, the refereed publication should be cited in addition to or instead of the preprint version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of contemporaneous work (3-month rule) for comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: For comparison, papers (whether refereed or not) appearing less than 3 months before the submission deadline should be considered contemporaneous to the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relieves authors from the obligation to make detailed comparisons that require additional experimentation and/or in-depth analysis, but they are still expected to cite and discuss contemporaneous work to the degree feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer guidance when authors miss citing recent preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should give authors the benefit of the doubt in cases where the work appears in preprints with no corresponding refereed publication, especially preprints that are recent and/or not widely cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases, reviewers should point authors to the non-cited work (so that they can discuss it in the camera-ready version) but not penalize the authors for missing the citation. Nonetheless, failure to cite relevant prior work or failure to compare to (non-contemporaneous) empirical results may affect assessment.
